# abstractcode-tui

> abstractcode-tui is a reactive terminal client for the AbstractGateway
> control plane, built on the AbstractTUI rendering engine. The coding agent
> runs durably on the gateway; this binary starts runs, streams their
> ledgers live (SSE with a polling fallback), renders reasoning cycles,
> tool cards that update in place, markdown answers and generated images,
> resolves tool-approval and ask-user waits through focus-trapped modals
> (with a persisted read/write/all auto-approval tier plus per-tool pins),
> steers the agent mid-run, queues follow-up prompts, attaches files to
> prompts (`/attach`, a file browser, or drag & drop onto the terminal —
> uploaded at send as `context.attachments`), and keeps a durable
> session whose history the gateway replays server-side. It also talks
> with gateway-hosted summoned entities: `@name` opens a durable visit
> with its own transcript and header chip (turns are non-interruptible,
> rendered honestly). One crate, three dependencies (abstracttui, ureq,
> serde_json). MIT licensed.

## Core docs

- [README](README.md): The pitch, a rendered-screen sketch, install,
  quickstart, the workspace-policy note, and how this client relates to the
  Python `abstractcode` CLI.
- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): Install to first run —
  `login`, `doctor`, the first approval, steering, sessions, workflows,
  workspaces, themes, working with entities, approval tiers, and headless
  one-shots.
- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): The thin-client design — threading
  contract (UI thread owns signals; a worker owns HTTP; WakeHandle posts),
  the ledger fold, SSE/polling transports, wait resolution, module map,
  testing model, honest limits.
- [Reference](docs/api.md): Every CLI option and env var, slash commands
  (including `@name`, `/entities`, `/task`, `/end`, `/queue`, `/goal`,
  `/permissions`, `/workspace`, `/attach`, `/export`, `/context`, `/gpu`,
  `/redraw`), key bindings (incl. `Ctrl+L` repaint, `Ctrl+J` newline,
  `Ctrl+O` drop-undo, `Alt+E` conversation focus, the composer's editor
  chords, `?` reference), the type-to-focus rule (typing, pasting or
  dropping a file returns focus to the composer and keeps the input),
  per-modal keys, transcript glyph
  vocabulary, attachments custody rules, exec exit codes, and prompt-cache
  posture (`exec --no-prompt-cache`, its scope, and how to verify the lane).
- [FAQ](docs/faq.md): Durability, workspace policy, token stats, steering
  semantics, queue pause semantics, approval tiers, parallel sessions,
  prompt-cache A/B.
- [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md): Symptom → cause → fix for
  connection, auth, catalog, provider, workspace, and rendering issues.
- [Orchestration cards](docs/orchestration-cards.md): One card per coding
  workflow accepted by `--workflow` — anatomy, how each decides it is done,
  what it remembers, measured profile, and when to choose it.
- [Documentation index](docs/README.md): One-line map of every page.

## Project

- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): Release history (0.1.0 was the first release —
  and the first application built on AbstractTUI; 0.2.0 is the engine-0.2.0
  adoption wave: Feed transcript, multiline composer + completion, in-app
  selection/copy, engine follow-tail and intervals; 0.3.0 is the
  control-and-collaboration wave: prompt queue, /goal client half,
  @entity conversations, tiered tool approvals, /workspace scope; 0.4.0
  is the conclusion + presence wave: offloaded/failed-answer conclusion
  fixes, header facts + instrument footer, /context declared window,
  /gpu meter, Ctrl+L//redraw screen recovery — engine-owned full redraw
  + redraw-on-focus-gained since abstracttui 0.2.6).
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): Build/test gates, the layering rules
  (signal ownership, pure protocol layer, replay-safe fold), which test to
  write for which change.
- [Security policy](SECURITY.md): Private reporting; credentials at rest
  (0600 login store) and in transit; untrusted-render-input scope.
- [Acknowledgements](ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS.md): The three dependencies and the
  sibling projects (AbstractGateway, the Python abstractcode).
- [License](LICENSE): MIT.

## Code entry points

- [src/lib.rs](src/lib.rs): Crate root with the layer map and `run_cli`.
- [src/protocol.rs](src/protocol.rs): Pure extraction over gateway ledger
  records — the protocol contract in one file.
- [src/transcript.rs](src/transcript.rs): The fold from records to
  transcript items, stats, and pending waits.
- [src/runner.rs](src/runner.rs): The worker thread owning every HTTP call
  and per-run stream thread.
- [src/ui/](src/ui/mod.rs): AbstractTUI views — chrome, transcript pane,
  modals.
- [tests/headless_ui.rs](tests/headless_ui.rs): The real interface driven
  through AbstractTUI's capture harness (the pattern for UI tests).
- [scripts/pty_live_smoke.py](scripts/pty_live_smoke.py): Live end-to-end
  proof against a running gateway.
